NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Visitors offer rich gifts but expect a say in the village's decisions: welcome them without the gift, or accept with care.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Visitors from a powerful island have brought the village wonderful gifts: tools, cloth and dried fruit. In return, they would like a seat at the village gathering. (subject) says hospitality is free, but the gathering is not for sale. (friend) says one seat is a small price. What should the village answer?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) thanks the visitors warmly, feeds them and sends them home with the gifts. The gathering stays the village's own. The visitors are puzzled, and come back the next year without gifts, just to visit.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The village accepts, on the condition that the visitors' seat can speak but never decide. The visitors agree. Over the years, they push and push, and the village holds the line. It is tiring. The tools are good.
